legend: Tiago was playing the famous Directed Bank game with his friends Leonardo, Gabriel, and Paulo.

As everyone knows, the Directed Bank board has N$$$N$$$ positions and M$$$M$$$ possible moves, with the i$$$i$$$-th move represented by the tuple (Ui,Vi,Wi)$$$(U_i, V_i, W_i)$$$; that is, if the player is on position Ui$$$U_i$$$, they can move to position Vi$$$V_i$$$, adding Wi$$$W_i$$$ to their balance. It's possible for the balance to become negative during the game.
The game always starts from position number 1, and in a round, the player can make a valid move or wait on the same spot, without losing or gaining anything.

Being an expert Directed Bank player, Tiago soon discovers a bug feature in the game! It's possible to accumulate infinite money! But it's not so clear how this could happen, and Leonardo and Gabriel disagreed with the statement, demanding proof. Tiago said he would demonstrate with an example of infinite moves during the game, which would also take an infinitely long time.
But since the pizza they ordered was almost arriving, there was only enough time for Tiago to play a finite number of rounds, and the problem remained open.
Knowing that you are a great programmer and that you are training for the UFPE Programming Contest, Paulo proposed you a challenge: prove or disprove Tiago!

But since infinity is a very long time, you only need to simulate 10998244353$$$10^{998244353}$$$ rounds to convince the group of friends. That is, given the description of the board, state the largest possible average value per round that can be obtained on this board after 10998244353$$$10^{998244353}$$$ rounds.
input: The first line of input contains two integers 2≤N≤2000$$$2 \le N \le 2000$$$, 1≤M≤2000$$$1 \le M \le 2000$$$, representing the number of positions on the board and the number of possible valid moves.

The following M$$$M$$$ lines contain three integers Ui,Vi,Wi$$$U_i, V_i, W_i$$$, with 1≤Ui,Vi≤N$$$1 \le U_i, V_i \le N$$$ and −109≤Wi≤109$$$-10^9 \le W_i \le 10^9$$$, where Ui≠Vi$$$U_i \neq V_i$$$. This represents the list of valid moves.
Note that multiple edges between the same pair of positions are allowed.
output: Print a real number, the answer to the problem. Your solution will be considered correct if it has a relative or absolute error less than or equal to 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$.
note: In sample 1, a valid strategy is to go from square 1 to square 2, return to square 1, then go to square 2, and so on (1,2,1,2,1,2,…)$$$(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, \ldots)$$$. After infinite rounds, the average points accumulated per round will be 0.5$$$0.5$$$.
In sample 2, a valid strategy is to never leave the first square, thus never losing points in the balance.

legend.ai: Tiago 正在和他的朋友 Leonardo、Gabriel 以及 Paulo 一起玩著名的 Directed Bank 游戏。
众所周知，Directed Bank 的棋盘有 N$$$N$$$ 个位置和 M$$$M$$$ 种可能的移动，第 i$$$i$$$ 次移动用三元组 (Ui,Vi,Wi)$$$(U_i, V_i, W_i)$$$ 表示；也就是说，如果玩家位于位置 Ui$$$U_i$$$，就可以移动到位置 Vi$$$V_i$$$，并将 Wi$$$W_i$$$ 加到余额中。游戏过程中余额可能变为负数。
游戏总是从编号为 1 的位置开始。在一回合中，玩家可以进行一次合法移动，或者停留在原地，且余额不会增加或减少。
作为一名经验丰富的 Directed Bank 玩家，Tiago 很快发现了游戏中的一个漏洞特性！竟然有可能积累无限多的钱！但这如何发生并不明确，Leonardo 和 Gabriel 不同意这一说法，要求给出证明。Tiago 说他将通过展示游戏中无限次移动的例子来证明，而这也将花费无限长的时间。
不过，由于他们点的披萨马上就要送到了，Tiago 只有足够的时间进行有限回合的游戏，因此问题仍未解决。
知道你是一名优秀的程序员，并且正在为 UFPE 编程竞赛训练，Paulo 向你提出挑战：证明或反驳 Tiago！
不过，由于无限长时间太久了，你只需模拟 10998244353$$$10^{998244353}$$$ 个回合就能说服这群朋友。也就是说，给定棋盘的描述，求在经过 10998244353$$$10^{998244353}$$$ 个回合后，在该棋盘上能够获得的每回合平均值的最大可能值。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含两个整数 2≤N≤2000$$$2 \le N \le 2000$$$、1≤M≤2000$$$1 \le M \le 2000$$$，分别表示棋盘上的位置数量和可能的有效移动数量。
接下来的 M$$$M$$$ 行包含三个整数 Ui、Vi、Wi$$$U_i, V_i, W_i$$$，其中 1≤Ui,Vi≤N$$$1 \le U_i, V_i \le N$$$ 且 −109≤Wi≤109$$$-10^9 \le W_i \le 10^9$$$，并且 Ui≠Vi$$$U_i \neq V_i$$$。这些整数表示有效移动的列表。
注意，同一对位置之间允许存在多条边。

output.ai: 输出一个实数，即该问题的答案。如果相对误差或绝对误差小于或等于 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$，则你的解法将被视为正确。

note.ai: 在样例 1 中，一种有效策略是从方格 1 走到方格 2，返回方格 1，然后再走到方格 2，如此往复(1,2,1,2,1,2,…)$$$(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, \ldots)$$$。经过无限轮次后，每轮累积的平均得分将为 0.5$$$0.5$$$。
在样例 2 中，一种有效策略是永远不离开第一个方格，因此不会损失积分。
